tagline: and the controls around the model.
hero.sub: I build and test AI systems in the open: an approval-gated support workflow, an agent runtime and evaluation harnesses, each with its evidence and its limits published.

explains.ai: An agent that only sounds right is a liability. I keep the loop explicit (plan, tool, observation) and check the whole trace before an answer counts.
explains.data: Streaming bugs hide in time. I model event time and a watermark explicitly, so late data is handled or dropped on purpose, never by accident.
explains.product: A funnel is arithmetic until it drives a decision. Here every rate is an input, so you can see which stage is actually worth fixing.
explains.maref: LLM outputs can look correct while still being unsupported. MAREF is my attempt to separate the ways an agent can fail instead of averaging them away.
explains.realtime-streaming-pipeline: Fraud signals decay in minutes. I used explainable rules so every flag can be inspected, and event-time windows with a watermark so late data cannot grow state forever.
explains.spark-data-lakehouse: Bad rows should fail loudly between layers, not surface in a dashboard. Each medallion layer has one job, and quality checks sit at the boundaries.
explains.llm-eval-framework: LLM outputs can look correct while being unsupported. llmeval keeps weighted scores and hard thresholds separate, so a good average cannot hide a failed grounding check.
explains.genai-doc-assistant: A fluent answer is not enough; it needs a path back to its source. The default reader is extractive, so it can only quote what was retrieved, and it abstains otherwise.
explains.mlops-platform: Models get trained once and forgotten. Registry stages and PSI/KS drift checks keep the model's lifecycle and its inputs visible.
explains.experimentation-toolkit: Most A/B tests ship on noise. The toolkit sizes a test before it runs, and checks guardrails before it calls a win.
